newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes lower after sell off in silver.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes lower after sell off in silver.

text.p: Precious metals turned lower on Friday led by a drop in silver which was hit by speculative selling in New York.
Gold, sentiment towards it shredded by news that the conservative Germans may revalue their reserves in a move linked to their buget deficit, sank with silver.
Gold slipped to a London fix at $344.50 an ounce, down $2.50 from the morning and against $346.40 on Thursday.
It fell through support at $345 to turn at $343.50 as bargain hunters arrived.
Silver had been ignored in the last few days, with the focus on gold and after it had bounced up to its highest fixing since April 2 this year at $4.8735 on Wednesday.
It eased to $4.7173 during London's Friday afternoon.
"Silver was sold into as soon as New York opened. The funds came in and that was it," said one London-based dealer.
The New York Comex July silver futures contract was down 15.3 cents at 470.50 cents shortly after the gold fixing when the June gold contract was $3.10 down at $342.10.
Frail market confidence has been sternly tested since Wednesday night when rumours that Germany was considering revaluing its gold reserves first emerged.
"This is a structural change for the market," said Union Bank of Switzerland bullion market analyst Andy Smith.
The proposal comes as an additional gap of over 18 billion marks was revealed in Germany's 1997 budget.
The difference between Germany revaluing its reserves and other European countries doing the same thing over the past two decades was linking it to a budget problem, Smith said.
Dealers said the long term risk for the market was that gold would now be treated like any other asset which would be sold if it didn't earn its keep.
Technically gold had been looking weaker having failed to make progress on a relatively bullish chart pattern earlier in the week, dealers said.
Platinum and palladium came off with silver too. Platinum tried and failed to get through $400.00 an ounce and palladium turned back after a four-year high at $174.50 this week.

But the rare white metals remain relatively firm. Even news that Russia expected to begin export talks with the Japanese trade houses - delayed since the start of the year - failed to take the heat out of prices.
Platinum was down $1.75 at $391.00/$392.00 and palladium off $1.20 at $171.30/$172.30.
